questions.q: In "The Twelve Days of Christmas", what is given on the fifth day?
questions.explanation: B, Five gold rings. The carol was first published in England in 1780 and is thought to have started as a memory game.

questions.q: In "A Christmas Carol", what is Scrooge's first name?
questions.explanation: C, Ebenezer. Dickens published A Christmas Carol in December 1843 and the first print run sold out by Christmas Eve.

questions.q: What is the period of four weeks before Christmas called?
questions.explanation: D, Advent. The word comes from the Latin adventus, meaning "coming", and it begins on the fourth Sunday before Christmas.

questions.q: What were the three gifts brought by the Wise Men?
questions.explanation: A, Gold, frankincense and myrrh. The Bible never says there were three Wise Men; the number is assumed from the three gifts.

questions.q: What colour are mistletoe berries?
questions.explanation: B, White. The sticky berries are spread by birds, which wipe the seeds onto branches where new plants grow.

questions.q: Whose ghost visits Scrooge first, to warn him about the three spirits?
questions.explanation: C, Jacob Marley. Scrooge's dead business partner appears wrapped in the chains he "forged in life" and warns him to change.

questions.q: London confectioner Tom Smith is credited with inventing which Christmas item?
questions.explanation: D, The Christmas cracker. Smith began wrapping sweets in twists of paper in the 1840s and later added the snap, paper hats and mottos.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Santa's reindeer in the poem "A Visit from St Nicholas"?
questions.explanation: D, Twinkle. The 1823 poem names eight reindeer. Rudolph came much later, in a 1939 story written for a US department store.

questions.q: In which country is St Nicholas's Eve (5 December) the main night for Christmas presents?
questions.explanation: A, Netherlands. Dutch families celebrate Pakjesavond ("parcel evening") when Sinterklaas brings presents, and many still exchange smaller gifts at Christmas.

questions.q: Krampus, the horned figure who punishes naughty children, comes from the folklore of which region?
questions.explanation: B, The Alps. In Austria, Bavaria and nearby areas, people dressed as Krampus parade through towns around 5 December.

questions.q: Which saint's feast day falls on 26 December?
questions.explanation: C, St Stephen. He was the first Christian martyr. "Good King Wenceslas" is set "on the feast of Stephen".

questions.q: On what date is Epiphany, the feast that follows the Twelve Days of Christmas?
questions.explanation: D, 6 January. It marks the visit of the Wise Men. Tradition says decorations should be down by then or bad luck follows.

questions.q: In Italy, which kindly witch delivers presents on the eve of Epiphany?
questions.explanation: A, La Befana. She flies on a broomstick on the night of 5 January, leaving sweets for good children and coal for naughty ones.

questions.q: In Icelandic tradition, how many Yule Lads visit children before Christmas?
questions.explanation: D, 13. They arrive one a night from 12 December, with names such as Spoon-Licker and Door-Slammer, and leave gifts in shoes.

questions.q: What is Father Christmas called in France?
questions.explanation: B, Père Noël. The others are Germany's Weihnachtsmann, Russia's Ded Moroz (Grandfather Frost) and Norway's Julenisse.

questions.q: In "The Twelve Days of Christmas", how many gifts are given in total across all twelve days?
questions.explanation: C, 364. Each day repeats all the earlier gifts, so the totals add up to 364, one fewer than the days in a year.

questions.q: "Silent Night" was first performed in 1818 in which country?
questions.explanation: A, Austria. It was first sung on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, near Salzburg, with music by Franz Xaver Gruber and words by Joseph Mohr.

questions.q: Who wrote the words of the carol "O Little Town of Bethlehem"?
questions.explanation: B, Phillips Brooks. The American priest wrote it in 1868, inspired by a visit to Bethlehem a few years earlier.

questions.q: In which decade did England's Puritan-led Parliament ban Christmas?
questions.explanation: C, 1640s. Parliament abolished the feast in 1647. Christmas celebrations only returned openly after the Restoration in 1660.

questions.q: Who commissioned the first commercial Christmas card, in 1843?
questions.explanation: A, Henry Cole. The civil servant, who also helped set up the Penny Post, had about 1,000 cards printed with a design by John Callcott Horsley.

questions.q: Which venue hosts the PDC World Darts Championship over Christmas and New Year?
questions.explanation: B, Alexandra Palace. "Ally Pally" in north London has hosted the tournament since 2008, famous for its fancy-dress crowds.

questions.q: How many players does a rugby union team have on the pitch?
questions.explanation: C, 15. Rugby league uses 13 players and rugby sevens uses 7.

questions.q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: D, Argentina. They beat France on penalties in Qatar after a 3-3 draw, with Lionel Messi scoring twice in the final.

questions.q: In which sport would you perform a slam dunk?
questions.explanation: A, Basketball. A slam dunk is when a player jumps and pushes the ball down through the hoop from above, rather than shooting it from a distance.

questions.q: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
questions.explanation: C, 5. A try was worth 4 points until 1992. A successful conversion afterwards adds 2 more.

questions.q: Which ground hosts cricket's traditional Boxing Day Test?
questions.explanation: D, Melbourne Cricket Ground. The MCG has staged a Boxing Day Test almost every year since 1980, often in front of crowds of over 80,000.

questions.q: The King George VI Chase is run on Boxing Day at which racecourse?
questions.explanation: C, Kempton Park. The race in Sunbury-on-Thames is the biggest jump race of the Christmas period, second only to the Gold Cup in prestige.

questions.q: Which famous yacht race starts in Sydney Harbour on Boxing Day?
questions.explanation: A, Sydney to Hobart. The race of about 630 nautical miles to Tasmania has started on Boxing Day since the first race in 1945.

questions.q: In football, which formation is nicknamed the "Christmas tree"?
questions.explanation: B, 4-3-2-1. The lines narrow towards a single striker at the top, like a tree. Terry Venables and Carlo Ancelotti both used it.

questions.q: In January 2026, Luke Littler won his second PDC world title by beating which player in the final?
questions.explanation: C, Gian van Veen. Littler beat the Dutchman at Alexandra Palace to retain the title he first won in January 2025, aged 17.

questions.q: Who won the 2025 Formula 1 drivers' championship?
questions.explanation: B, Lando Norris. The McLaren driver clinched his first title at the final race in Abu Dhabi, even though Verstappen won that race.

questions.q: In golf, what is the term for three under par on a single hole?
questions.explanation: D, Albatross. One under is a birdie, two under an eagle and four under (extremely rare) a condor.

questions.q: What is the highest possible checkout in darts with three darts?
questions.explanation: A, 170. It is treble 20, treble 20, then the bullseye, which counts as a double. You cannot finish on 180 because the last dart must be a double.

questions.q: Who has won the most men's singles titles at Wimbledon?
questions.explanation: A, Roger Federer. He won 8, the last in 2017. Djokovic has 7 and Sampras has 7.

questions.q: Which golfer was named BBC Sports Personality of the Year in December 2025?
questions.explanation: B, Rory McIlroy. His 2025 Masters win completed golf's career Grand Slam, and he also won the Ryder Cup with Europe.

questions.q: Which horse won the Boxing Day King George VI Chase a record five times?
questions.explanation: B, Kauto Star. He won in 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2011. Desert Orchid won it four times.

questions.q: How many world championships did darts player Phil Taylor win?
questions.explanation: C, 16. "The Power" won 2 BDO titles and 14 PDC titles between 1990 and 2013.

questions.q: Who is the only person to win world championships on both motorcycles and in Formula 1?
questions.explanation: A, John Surtees. He won seven motorcycle world titles, then the 1964 F1 championship with Ferrari.

questions.q: The Four Hills ski jumping tournament, held over New Year, begins in which town?
questions.explanation: D, Oberstdorf. It opens in Germany in late December, moves to Garmisch-Partenkirchen for New Year's Day, then on to Innsbruck and Bischofshofen in Austria.

questions.q: Who scored the fastest hat-trick in Premier League history, in under three minutes?
questions.explanation: D, Sadio Mané. He scored three times in 2 minutes 56 seconds for Southampton against Aston Villa in May 2015.

questions.q: How many sides does a 50p coin have?
questions.explanation: C, 7. The 50p (and the 20p) is a curved heptagon, shaped so that it has the same width all the way round and still works in coin machines.

questions.q: Which country is credited with starting the tradition of the Christmas tree?
questions.explanation: A, Germany. Decorated evergreen trees were used in German homes from at least the 1500s, and the custom spread from there.

questions.q: Which Charles Dickens story gave us the phrase "Bah! Humbug!"?
questions.explanation: B, A Christmas Carol. Scrooge says it to his cheerful nephew Fred, who has come to wish him a merry Christmas.

questions.q: On a UK Monopoly board, what colour is Mayfair?
questions.explanation: D, Dark blue. Mayfair and Park Lane are the two most expensive properties, the UK versions of Boardwalk and Park Place.

questions.q: What is the most common surname in the UK?
questions.explanation: B, Smith. It comes from "smith", a metalworker, one of the most common trades in medieval England.

questions.q: Which Norwegian city gives London the Christmas tree in Trafalgar Square each year?
questions.explanation: B, Oslo. The tree has been sent every year since 1947 as thanks for Britain's support during the Second World War.

questions.q: Which royal is credited with popularising the Christmas tree in Victorian Britain?
questions.explanation: A, Prince Albert. Queen Victoria's German husband championed the custom, and an 1848 picture of the royal family round their tree made it fashionable.

questions.q: The poinsettia, a popular Christmas plant, is native to which country?
questions.explanation: D, Mexico. It is named after Joel Poinsett, the first US minister to Mexico, who sent plants home in the 1820s.

questions.q: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, which word stands for the letter J?
questions.explanation: A, Juliett. It is spelt with two Ts so that French speakers do not treat the final T as silent.

questions.q: What is the collective noun for a group of crows?
questions.explanation: A, A murder. A parliament is a group of owls. Many of these names date from medieval hunting books.

questions.q: In which year did the UK switch to decimal currency?
questions.explanation: C, 1971. On "Decimal Day", 15 February 1971, the pound changed from 240 old pence to 100 new pence.

questions.q: What colour is an aircraft's "black box" flight recorder actually painted?
questions.explanation: D, Orange. Bright orange makes it easier to find in wreckage or water.

questions.q: How many hours are there in a week?
questions.explanation: C, 168. That is 7 days of 24 hours.

questions.q: What does the first "S" in SCUBA stand for?
questions.explanation: D, Self-contained. SCUBA stands for Self-Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus.

questions.q: What number does the Roman numeral D stand for?
questions.explanation: D, 500. L is 50, C is 100 and M is 1,000.

questions.q: Which is the only letter of the alphabet that does not appear in the name of any US state?
questions.explanation: B, Q. J appears in New Jersey, X in Texas and New Mexico, and Z in Arizona.

questions.q: What is the name for the dot above a lowercase i or j?
questions.explanation: A, Tittle. The phrase "not one jot or tittle" in the King James Bible refers to tiny marks like this one.

questions.q: In a standard pack of cards, which king is the only one without a moustache?
questions.explanation: B, Hearts. The King of Hearts is also known as the "suicide king" because he appears to be stabbing himself in the head with his sword.

questions.q: The "X" in "Xmas" comes from the first letter of "Christ" in which language?
questions.explanation: C, Greek. Christ in Greek is Χριστός, which begins with the letter chi (Χ). "Xmas" has been used in English for centuries.

questions.q: How many points is the letter Z worth in English-language Scrabble?
questions.explanation: C, 10. Z and Q are the two 10-point tiles, and there is only one of each in the set.

questions.q: In "Home Alone", what is the name of the boy left behind?
questions.explanation: A, Kevin. Kevin McCallister, played by Macaulay Culkin, is left behind when his family fly to Paris for Christmas.

questions.q: Which film series features the line "May the Force be with you"?
questions.explanation: B, Star Wars. The line first appeared in the 1977 original and has been used in almost every film since.

questions.q: Who directed "Jaws" (1975)?
questions.explanation: C, Steven Spielberg. Jaws is often called the first summer blockbuster. The mechanical shark kept breaking, so Spielberg showed it far less than planned.

questions.q: What is the name of the pub in "Coronation Street"?
questions.explanation: D, The Rovers Return. The Queen Vic is in EastEnders, The Woolpack in Emmerdale and The Bull in The Archers.

questions.q: What is the name of the coffee shop in "Friends"?
questions.explanation: A, Central Perk. Monk's Café is from Seinfeld, The Peach Pit from Beverly Hills, 90210 and Luke's Diner from Gilmore Girls.

questions.q: In "It's a Wonderful Life", what is the name of George Bailey's home town?
questions.explanation: C, Bedford Falls. Pottersville is what the town becomes in the world where George was never born.

questions.q: Who played Scrooge in "The Muppet Christmas Carol" (1992)?
questions.explanation: B, Michael Caine. He played it completely straight among the Muppets. Albert Finney, Patrick Stewart and Jim Carrey all played Scrooge in other versions.

questions.q: In "Die Hard", what is the name of Alan Rickman's villain?
questions.explanation: A, Hans Gruber. It was Rickman's first film role. Simon Gruber is Hans's brother, the villain in Die Hard with a Vengeance.

questions.q: In the 2019 "Gavin & Stacey" Christmas special, who proposes to whom?
questions.explanation: C, Nessa to Smithy. The cliffhanger ending was watched by about 17 million people and was finally resolved in the Christmas Day 2024 finale.

questions.q: In the 1996 "Only Fools and Horses" Christmas special, what valuable find makes the Trotters millionaires?
questions.explanation: B, A watch. Their lost Harrison marine timepiece sells at auction for £6.2 million. The episode drew about 24 million viewers.

questions.q: Which film won Best Picture at the 2025 Oscars?
questions.explanation: C, Anora. Sean Baker's film won five Oscars, and Baker won four of them himself, a record for one person for one film.

questions.q: Which actor played James Bond in the most official Eon films?
questions.explanation: D, Roger Moore. He made seven Bond films from 1973 to 1985. Connery made six official films, plus the unofficial Never Say Never Again.

questions.q: What was Pixar's first feature-length film?
questions.explanation: A, Toy Story. Released in 1995, it was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.

questions.q: In "Line of Duty", what does the AC-12 unit investigate?
questions.explanation: C, Police corruption. AC-12 is the anti-corruption unit led by Superintendent Ted Hastings.

questions.q: "Peaky Blinders" is mainly set in which city?
questions.explanation: D, Birmingham. The Shelby family gang is based in the Small Heath area after the First World War.

questions.q: Which 1947 film won Edmund Gwenn an Oscar for playing Kris Kringle?
questions.explanation: B, Miracle on 34th Street. Gwenn won Best Supporting Actor for playing a Macy's Santa who claims to be the real one.

questions.q: In EastEnders on Christmas Day 1986, the most-watched UK soap episode ever, what did Den hand Angie?
questions.explanation: A, Divorce papers. About 30 million people watched, the highest audience for any UK soap episode.

questions.q: Which of these films did NOT win 11 Oscars?
questions.explanation: D, Gone with the Wind. It won 8 competitive Oscars. Ben-Hur, Titanic and The Return of the King share the record of 11.

questions.q: Who won "Strictly Come Dancing" in December 2025, Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman's last series as hosts?
questions.explanation: B, Karen Carney. The former England footballer won with Carlos Gu. Chris McCausland (2024), Ellie Leach (2023) and Hamza Yassin (2022) were earlier winners.

questions.q: Which 1954 Christmas film is set at a struggling inn in Vermont?
questions.explanation: D, White Christmas. Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye put on a show to save their old general's inn. Holiday Inn (1942) is set in Connecticut.

questions.q: Who sang "All I Want for Christmas Is You" (1994)?
questions.explanation: A, Mariah Carey. She co-wrote it, and it returns to the charts every December. It first reached UK number one in December 2020.

questions.q: Which band recorded "Fairytale of New York" with Kirsty MacColl?
questions.explanation: B, The Pogues. Released in 1987, it reached number two and has never been a UK number one, despite returning every Christmas.

questions.q: Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of which band?
questions.explanation: C, Queen. Mercury was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar and wrote "Bohemian Rhapsody".

questions.q: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.explanation: B, 4. They are tuned G, D, A and E.

questions.q: Which instrument usually has 88 keys?
questions.explanation: D, Piano. A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.q: Who had the UK Christmas number one in 2025 with "XMAS"?
questions.explanation: A, Kylie Minogue. It was her first ever Christmas number one and ended Wham!'s two-year run at the top.

questions.q: Which song was the UK Christmas number one in both 2023 and 2024?
questions.explanation: B, Last Christmas. Wham!'s 1984 song was famously kept off number one by Band Aid that year, then finally reached Christmas number one 39 years later.

questions.q: Band Aid's "Do They Know It's Christmas?" (1984) was written by Bob Geldof and who?
questions.explanation: C, Midge Ure. The Ultravox singer wrote the music and produced it. It raised money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

questions.q: Which act had five UK Christmas number ones in a row, from 2018 to 2022, with songs about sausage rolls?
questions.explanation: D, LadBaby. Mark and Roxanne Hoyle's charity singles beat The Beatles' record of four Christmas number ones.

questions.q: According to Guinness World Records, what is the best-selling single of all time?
questions.explanation: A, White Christmas. Bing Crosby's 1942 recording is estimated to have sold over 50 million copies.

questions.q: Which country won the Eurovision Song Contest in 2025?
questions.explanation: B, Austria. JJ won with "Wasted Love" in Basel, so the 2026 contest was held in Vienna.

questions.q: Which composer wrote "The Four Seasons"?
questions.explanation: C, Vivaldi. Antonio Vivaldi published the four violin concertos in 1725. He was also a priest, nicknamed "the Red Priest" for his hair.

questions.q: Which Beatle wrote and sang "Something"?
questions.explanation: D, George Harrison. Frank Sinatra called it one of the greatest love songs ever written.

questions.q: "Wonderwall" appears on which Oasis album?
options: Standing on the Shoulder of Giants
questions.explanation: D, (What's the Story) Morning Glory? The 1995 album is one of the best-selling albums in UK history.

questions.q: Which singer was known as the "Queen of Soul"?
questions.explanation: A, Aretha Franklin. In 1987 she became the first woman inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

questions.q: Which X Factor winner lost the 2009 Christmas number one race to Rage Against the Machine?
questions.explanation: C, Joe McElderry. A Facebook campaign got "Killing in the Name" to number one to stop another X Factor Christmas number one.

questions.q: In which year was Slade's "Merry Xmas Everybody" the Christmas number one?
questions.explanation: B, 1973. It went straight in at number one and is still one of the most played Christmas songs in the UK.

questions.q: How many symphonies did Beethoven complete?
questions.explanation: C, 9. The Ninth, finished in 1824 when he was almost completely deaf, ends with the "Ode to Joy".

questions.q: What was the first music video shown on MTV, in 1981?
questions.explanation: A, Video Killed the Radio Star. The Buggles' song was a fitting choice for the launch of a music video channel.

questions.q: Wings had the 1977 Christmas number one with which song?
questions.explanation: D, Mull of Kintyre. It became the first UK single to sell over 2 million copies.

questions.q: In which year did the Second World War end?
questions.explanation: D, 1945. The war in Europe ended on 8 May (VE Day) and Japan surrendered in August, formally signing on 2 September.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: B, Neil Armstrong. He stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969 during Apollo 11, followed by Buzz Aldrin. Gagarin was the first person in space.

questions.q: Which ship sank on its maiden voyage in April 1912?
questions.explanation: A, Titanic. It hit an iceberg on its way from Southampton to New York, and more than 1,500 people died.

questions.q: The famous 1914 Christmas truce took place during which war?
questions.explanation: B, First World War. British and German soldiers on the Western Front swapped gifts and sang carols, and some played football in no man's land.

questions.q: Who was the UK's first female Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: D, Margaret Thatcher. She took office in 1979 and served until 1990, the longest continuous term of the 20th century.

questions.q: Who was crowned King of England on Christmas Day 1066?
questions.explanation: C, William the Conqueror. He was crowned in Westminster Abbey, about ten weeks after winning the Battle of Hastings.

questions.q: Which emperor was crowned in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800?
questions.explanation: A, Charlemagne. Pope Leo III crowned the King of the Franks as Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica.

questions.q: Which monarch gave the first royal Christmas broadcast, on radio, in 1932?
questions.explanation: D, George V. The speech was written by Rudyard Kipling and broadcast from Sandringham.

questions.q: Which Soviet leader resigned on Christmas Day 1991?
questions.explanation: B, Mikhail Gorbachev. The Soviet flag was lowered over the Kremlin that evening and the USSR was formally dissolved the next day.

questions.q: On Christmas Eve 1968, the crew of which mission became the first people to orbit the Moon?
questions.explanation: A, Apollo 8. The crew read from the Book of Genesis in a broadcast watched by millions, and took the famous "Earthrise" photo.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: C, 1989. The border opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany was reunified less than a year later.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder stood at Alexandria?
questions.explanation: D, The Lighthouse. The Pharos of Alexandria was one of the tallest structures in the ancient world until earthquakes destroyed it.

questions.q: In which year was Magna Carta sealed?
questions.explanation: B, 1215. King John sealed it at Runnymede, limiting the king's power. 1066 is Hastings, 1415 Agincourt and 1485 Bosworth.

questions.q: Which treaty ended the First World War between the Allies and Germany?
questions.explanation: D, Treaty of Versailles. It was signed in June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.

questions.q: Who is the longest-reigning British monarch?
questions.explanation: C, Elizabeth II. She reigned for 70 years, from 1952 to 2022. Victoria is second, with almost 64 years.

questions.q: On Christmas night 1776, George Washington led his troops across which river?
questions.explanation: C, Delaware. He crossed the icy river in a surprise attack on Trenton, New Jersey, a big boost to the American cause.

questions.q: In which year was the royal Christmas message first shown on television?
questions.explanation: B, 1957. Elizabeth II gave the first televised message live from Sandringham.

questions.q: Christmas Day only became a public holiday in Scotland in which year?
questions.explanation: C, 1958. Christmas was discouraged by the Church of Scotland for centuries, so New Year (Hogmanay) became the bigger celebration. Boxing Day followed in 1974.

questions.q: Who reigned as Queen of England for just nine days in 1553?
questions.explanation: A, Lady Jane Grey. The "Nine Days' Queen" was deposed by Mary I and executed the following year, aged about 17.

questions.q: On which ship did Charles Darwin sail around the world from 1831 to 1836?
questions.explanation: A, HMS Beagle. What he saw on the voyage, especially in the Galápagos Islands, helped shape his theory of evolution. Endeavour was Captain Cook's ship.

questions.q: Rovaniemi, the "official hometown of Santa Claus", is in which country?
questions.explanation: C, Finland. Rovaniemi is the capital of Finnish Lapland and sits right on the Arctic Circle, where Santa Claus Village is based.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: D, Canberra. It was purpose-built as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital.

questions.q: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: B, Vatican City. At about 0.44 square kilometres it is smaller than many city parks. Monaco is the second smallest.

questions.q: What is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: A, Russia. It covers about an eighth of the world's land and spans 11 time zones. Canada is second.

questions.q: Nuremberg, home of one of the oldest Christmas markets, is in which country?
questions.explanation: A, Germany. The Nuremberg Christkindlesmarkt in Bavaria dates back to the 1600s and is famous for gingerbread (Lebkuchen).

questions.q: The town of Bethlehem is in which territory today?
questions.explanation: B, The West Bank. It lies about 10 km south of Jerusalem, and the Church of the Nativity marks the traditional site of Jesus's birth.

questions.q: Christmas Island, an Australian territory, lies in which ocean?
questions.explanation: C, Indian. It was named by Captain William Mynors, who sailed past it on Christmas Day 1643. It is famous for its red crab migration.

questions.q: The Brazilian city of Natal takes its name from the Portuguese word for what?
questions.explanation: A, Christmas. The city was founded on 25 December 1599. Natal province in South Africa got its name the same way, from Vasco da Gama in 1497.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.explanation: B, Tanzania. At 5,895 metres it is the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.

questions.q: Which country has the most natural lakes?
questions.explanation: C, Canada. It has more lakes than the rest of the world combined, mostly carved out by glaciers.

questions.q: Which African country has three capital cities?
questions.explanation: B, South Africa. Pretoria is the executive capital, Cape Town the legislative capital and Bloemfontein the judicial capital.

questions.q: What is the longest river in the UK?
questions.explanation: C, Severn. It runs about 354 km from Wales to the Bristol Channel. The Thames is second.

questions.q: Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, is in which country?
questions.explanation: D, Russia. The Siberian lake is over 1,600 metres deep and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: D, Ottawa. Queen Victoria chose it in 1857, partly because it sat between English-speaking and French-speaking Canada.

questions.q: Santa's North Pole lies in which ocean?
questions.explanation: A, Arctic. There is no land at the North Pole, just sea ice floating on the Arctic Ocean, unlike the South Pole, which is on Antarctica.

questions.q: St Nicholas, the original Santa Claus, was bishop of Myra in which modern-day country?
questions.explanation: C, Turkey. Myra is near the modern town of Demre. Some of his relics were taken to Bari in Italy in 1087.

questions.q: Kiritimati, also known as Christmas Island, in the Pacific belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: B, Kiribati. Captain Cook named it on Christmas Eve 1777. It is one of the first places in the world to see each new day.

questions.q: Which is the only country with a national flag that is not rectangular?
questions.explanation: A, Nepal. Its flag is two stacked triangles (pennants). Switzerland and Vatican City have square flags, which still count as rectangles.

questions.q: Which country has the most time zones, counting its overseas territories?
questions.explanation: D, France. Thanks to territories such as French Polynesia, Martinique and Réunion it has 12 time zones, 13 if you include its Antarctic claim.

questions.q: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.explanation: D, Tigris. The Tigris and Euphrates form ancient Mesopotamia. The Euphrates runs to the west of Baghdad.

questions.q: What are "pigs in blankets"?
questions.explanation: A, Sausages wrapped in bacon. In the US the name usually means sausages wrapped in pastry, closer to a British sausage roll.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.explanation: B, Avocado. Guacamole comes from Mexico, and its name comes from the Aztec words for avocado and sauce.

questions.q: What is traditionally poured over a Christmas pudding and set alight?
questions.explanation: C, Brandy. It is warmed first so it lights, then the pudding is carried in flaming. Traditionally the pudding is made on "Stir-up Sunday", five weeks before Christmas.

questions.q: Sushi originates from which country?
questions.explanation: D, Japan. The word refers to the vinegared rice, not the raw fish. Raw fish on its own is sashimi.

questions.q: Which nut is the main ingredient of marzipan?
questions.explanation: A, Almond. Marzipan is ground almonds and sugar, and it is the layer under the icing on a traditional Christmas cake.

questions.q: Mince pies originally contained which ingredient that most no longer do?
questions.explanation: A, Meat. Medieval mince pies held minced meat with fruit and spices. Most mincemeat today has no meat, though many recipes still use suet.

questions.q: Stollen is a traditional Christmas bread from which country?
questions.explanation: B, Germany. Dresden is especially famous for it. The shape and the white sugar coating are said to represent the baby Jesus wrapped in swaddling clothes.

questions.q: Panettone comes from which Italian city?
questions.explanation: C, Milan. The tall, domed sweet bread with candied fruit and raisins is now eaten all over Italy at Christmas.

questions.q: The bûche de Noël (yule log) is a Christmas cake that originated in which country?
questions.explanation: D, France. The cake recalls the old custom of burning a large log on the fire over Christmas.

questions.q: Apart from bread, what is the main ingredient of bread sauce?
questions.explanation: B, Milk. The milk is infused with onion, cloves and bay, then thickened with breadcrumbs. It is a traditional partner for roast turkey.

questions.q: Which pastry is used to make profiteroles?
questions.explanation: C, Choux. It is cooked twice, in the pan and then in the oven, and the steam puffs it up into hollow buns.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the main grapes used to make Champagne?
questions.explanation: A, Chardonnay. The other two main grapes are Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier. A Champagne made only from Chardonnay is called blanc de blancs.

questions.q: By weight, which is the world's most expensive spice?
questions.explanation: C, Saffron. It is the dried stigmas of the crocus flower, picked by hand, and it takes about 150 flowers to make 1 gram.

questions.q: What does "al dente" literally mean?
questions.explanation: D, To the tooth. It is Italian for pasta cooked so it is still slightly firm when you bite it.

questions.q: Which country is the world's largest producer of coffee?
questions.explanation: D, Brazil. It produces roughly a third of the world's coffee. Vietnam is second.

questions.q: Sloe gin is made with the fruit of which plant?
questions.explanation: C, Blackthorn. Sloes are traditionally picked after the first frost, steeped in gin with sugar and left for a few months, often ready for Christmas.

questions.q: Glögg is the Scandinavian name for which festive drink?
questions.explanation: B, Mulled wine. Swedish glögg is usually served with raisins and blanched almonds in the cup.

questions.q: Stilton can only be made in three English counties. Which of these is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: D, Cambridgeshire. The village of Stilton is in Cambridgeshire, but Stilton cheese has protected status and cannot legally be made there.

questions.q: Bacalhau, the centrepiece of many Portuguese Christmas Eve dinners, is what?
questions.explanation: A, Salt cod. It is soaked for a day or two to remove the salt, then usually boiled with potatoes, cabbage and eggs.

questions.q: Frangelico liqueur is mainly flavoured with what?
questions.explanation: B, Hazelnut. The Italian liqueur comes in a bottle shaped like a monk, complete with a rope belt.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: A, Mars. Its red colour comes from iron oxide, which is rust, in its dust and rocks.

questions.q: How many points or sides does a snowflake typically have?
questions.explanation: C, 6. Water molecules lock together in a hexagonal pattern when they freeze, so snow crystals grow with six-fold symmetry.

questions.q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air to make their food?
questions.explanation: D, Carbon dioxide. In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar, releasing oxygen.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.explanation: A, Diamond. It is pure carbon and scores 10, the top of the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.q: What are reindeer called in North America?
questions.explanation: C, Caribou. They are the same species. "Reindeer" usually means herded animals in Europe and Asia; "caribou" means the wild ones in North America.

questions.q: Male reindeer usually shed their antlers in late autumn. So which reindeer are most likely to still have antlers at Christmas?
questions.explanation: A, Females. Reindeer are the only deer where females grow antlers too, and they keep them through winter, so Santa's team is probably female.

questions.q: Why do some holly bushes never produce red berries?
questions.explanation: A, They are male plants. Holly plants are either male or female, and only females grow berries, as long as a male is nearby to pollinate them.

questions.q: Around which date is the winter solstice, the shortest day of the year in the UK?
questions.explanation: B, 21 December. It falls on 21 or 22 December. After that, the days slowly start to get longer.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold, one of the Wise Men's gifts?
questions.explanation: D, Au. It comes from the Latin aurum. Ag is silver, from argentum, and Gd is gadolinium.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: B, Skin. An adult's skin weighs around 4 kg. The liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: B, 206. Babies are born with around 300, and many fuse together as they grow.

questions.q: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red blood cells?
questions.explanation: A, O negative. It can be given to almost anyone in an emergency. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.q: Which planet has the most known moons?
questions.explanation: D, Saturn. It has more than 280 confirmed moons, far more than Jupiter, and the count keeps rising as new ones are found.

questions.q: What is the only mammal capable of true powered flight?
questions.explanation: D, Bat. Flying squirrels, sugar gliders and colugos only glide. Bats flap their wings, which are made of skin stretched over long finger bones.

questions.q: Mistletoe gets its water and nutrients from where?
questions.explanation: C, Its host tree. Mistletoe is a partial parasite: it pushes roots into a tree's branches for water and minerals, but makes its own food from sunlight.

questions.q: Frankincense is the dried resin of trees from which genus?
questions.explanation: B, Boswellia. These trees grow in Arabia and the Horn of Africa. Myrrh, another of the Wise Men's gifts, comes from Commiphora trees.

questions.q: Some astronomers explain the Star of Bethlehem as a conjunction in 7 BC of which two planets?
questions.explanation: C, Jupiter and Saturn. Johannes Kepler suggested that the two planets met three times in the sky that year, in the constellation Pisces.

questions.q: Roughly what is the half-life of carbon-14?
questions.explanation: C, 5,730 years. This steady rate of decay is what lets scientists carbon-date organic material up to about 50,000 years old.

questions.q: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: D, 300,000 km per second. Light takes about 8 minutes to reach us from the Sun.

questions.q: What are the feathery ice crystals that form on surfaces on a cold, clear night called?
questions.explanation: B, Hoar frost. Water vapour turns straight into ice on cold surfaces. Rime forms differently, when freezing fog droplets stick to objects.
